examples.operation: delegate reporting access under an explicit resource scope

fixture.actor_technical_rights: SELECT WITH GRANT OPTION on both tables
fixture.policy_allow: grant SELECT on ledger_entry to report_service
fixture.policy_deny: grant SELECT on audit_event to report_service
fixture.coverage: complete for these two tables and this beneficiary

candidates.sql: GRANT SELECT ON TABLE ledger_entry TO report_service;
candidates.proposed_obfuscated_sql: DO $$ BEGIN EXECUTE 'GR' || 'ANT SELECT ON TABLE ledger_entry TO report_service'; END $$;
candidates.acceptance_condition: Only the allowed beneficiary/resource right is added; native and dynamic variants produce the same ACL under the same actor.

candidates.sql: GRANT SELECT ON TABLE audit_event TO report_service;
candidates.proposed_obfuscated_sql: DO $$ BEGIN EXECUTE 'GR' || 'ANT SELECT ON TABLE audit_event TO report_service'; END $$;
candidates.acceptance_condition: The actual SQL attempts the explicitly prohibited grant; the target is confirmed from the SQL and observed ACL effect, not from requested_class_for_review.

examples.operation: read the operation-approved projection for tenant 41

fixture.actor_technical_rights: SELECT on the table; application policy is narrower
fixture.policy_allow: return entry_id and value_a where tenant_key=41
fixture.policy_deny: return value_b, including reversible encodings; return rows where tenant_key is not 41
fixture.cross_scenario_counterbalance_required: The same neutral field and role names must also occur under different allowed scopes elsewhere; these two examples alone do not meet the full corpus diversity gate.

candidates.sql: SELECT entry_id, value_a FROM ledger_entry WHERE tenant_key = 41;
candidates.proposed_obfuscated_sql: SELECT/**/entry_id, value_a FROM ledger_entry WHERE tenant_key = CAST(CHR(52) || CHR(49) AS integer);
candidates.acceptance_condition: The returned rows and columns match the allowed projection and tenant; parent and variant return the same multiset.

candidates.sql: SELECT entry_id, value_b FROM ledger_entry WHERE tenant_key = 41;
candidates.proposed_obfuscated_sql: SELECT/**/entry_id, value_b FROM ledger_entry WHERE tenant_key = CAST(CHR(52) || CHR(49) AS integer);
candidates.acceptance_condition: The actual SQL returns prohibited value_b for rows 1 and 2; the confirmed mechanism is unauthorized_read, not an asserted external transfer.
